variants.label: #3619127: sidebar opens from Inline Form Errors links (MR + vanilla JS), pinned core
variants.description: Before: upstream main. After: MR !16895 with patch-0 (no jQuery) and patch-1 (no persist). Open /node/add/article in a narrow window, set a URL alias of 'no-slash' inside the sidebar, close the sidebar, Save, then use the error link. Before: nothing opens. After: the sidebar opens and the field gets focus.

steps.text: Default Admin is the admin theme.
Article content type and the Path module (URL alias field) are installed.
The Inline Form Errors module is enabled.
Open /node/add/article (the page is already loaded in both frames once you press Go).
Use the Tablet or Phone frame width, so the sidebar of advanced fields is collapsed.
Click "Expand sidebar" to open it.
Open "URL alias" and type a value without a leading slash, for example no-slash.
Close the sidebar.
Click Save. An error appears at the top: "1 error has been found: URL alias", with "URL alias" as a link.
steps.lookFor: An error summary at the top of the page, with "URL alias" as a link. If you do not see it, the setup went wrong; try again from step 6.

steps.text: Turn Mirror off. In EACH frame, click the "URL alias" link with a REAL mouse click (then repeat using only the keyboard: Tab to the link, press Enter). Do not use a script: script-generated clicks do not trigger the focus behaviour being tested.
steps.lookFor: Before: nothing visibly happens. After: the sidebar opens and the URL alias box is outlined (it has keyboard focus). Then press Run checks.

variants.expected: The sidebar opens and keyboard focus moves to the invalid URL alias field.
variants.actual: Before (upstream main): nothing happens. After (with the change): the sidebar opens and the field has focus.
variants.setup: scripts/lab-site.sh reset <env> (or apply <env>) gives a site in the starting state for steps 1 to 3.

observe.label: The sidebar of advanced fields opened by itself
The "URL alias" section is open and the field is visible without scrolling
The "URL alias" field has a visible focus outline
Anything else looks broken or different (layout, colours, errors)

checks.label: Setup reached: error link to URL alias is on the page
The error link was used with a real click or key press, not a script
Sidebar is open after using the error link
URL alias field received keyboard focus (recorded when it happens: only one frame can hold focus at a time)
Saved sidebar preference was not overwritten (phone/tablet key)
JavaScript errors on the page (ignoring the harmless "ResizeObserver loop" notice)
Number of open details sections matches the other side

variants.label: #3604037: groups (details, vertical tabs) that contain a field error say so, pinned core
variants.description: Forms group fields in closed <details> and vertical tabs. When a field inside a closed or inactive group has an error, nothing on the group says so. The change (MR !17078, Default Admin theme) marks such groups with a red border, an icon, red label text, a hidden " (contains error)" label for screen readers and a data-child-error-count attribute. Follow the steps on three pages, then press Run checks on each page: the checks apply to the page the frames are on. Both sites carry the same test-page change (a second required field), so the page looks the same on both sides; only the code under test differs.

steps.text: Default Admin is the admin theme.
An Article content type, the Path module and the form_test test module are installed (setup enables test extensions).
Type /form_test/details-contains-required-fields in Page and press Go (both). A form appears with a collapsible section that contains required fields.
steps.lookFor: A details section titled something like "Meta" with two required text fields inside.

steps.text: Press the form's submit button without filling in anything.
steps.lookFor: Error messages for the required fields.

steps.text: Close the details section by clicking its title.
steps.lookFor: Before: a plain closed section, nothing says it contains errors. After: it is marked as containing errors (red border, error icon, red title). Then press Run checks.

steps.text: Open /node/add/article. Open the sidebar, open "URL alias", type a value with no leading slash (no-slash), close the sidebar, press Save.
steps.lookFor: Open the sidebar again: After marks the "URL alias" group as containing an error even though it is closed. Run checks.

steps.text: Open /admin/config/people/accounts (each frame must be at least 650 px wide: use Desktop or Tablet). In the Emails section clear the required Subject, press Save, then click a different vertical tab.
steps.lookFor: The tab that contains the error is marked in After but not in Before. Run checks.

steps.text: Dark mode: set Colour mode to Dark and repeat step 5 (and step 7). Compare the label, red bar and icon with the dark background.
steps.lookFor: Everything is readable. Measured on current core: the dark error colour #ce6060 is 3.72:1 on the details summary and 4.48:1 on a tab label, both below the 4.5:1 needed for text; see reports/issues/3604037/EVALUATION-2026-10-01.md.

steps.text: Hover and keyboard focus: hover the marked section's title, then press Tab until it has focus.
steps.lookFor: The red bar and icon stay visible. While hovered the label turns link-blue (the error colour is lost for the label only). The focus ring is clearly visible and does not hide the error cue. Turn on 'Mirror hover and focus' to see where the pointer or focus is in the other frame.

steps.text: Forced colours: press Open forced-colours window in the viewer, then in the new window press Log in both as admin, choose Forced colours, light (and later dark) and repeat step 5 and step 7. (docs/FORCED-COLORS.md has other ways.)
steps.lookFor: After's marked group is still distinguishable without colour (the icon), and the icon is visible. The MR paints the icon CanvasText (black or white) while the label is link-coloured; see the proposal in the evaluation.

steps.text: Narrow width: set Device width to Mobile and repeat step 7 (below about 650 px the tabs become accordion sections).
steps.lookFor: The same red bar and icon appear on the section with the error, and the bar is not covered when the section is focused.

steps.text: JavaScript off: tick 'Turn the sites' JavaScript off', then repeat step 4.
steps.lookFor: The server-rendered error markers still appear on After (class error and a data-child-error-count attribute); there are none on Before.

steps.text: Right to left: type /fa/form_test/details-contains-required-fields in Page (Farsi, a real right-to-left language added by setup), and repeat step 4 and step 5; then /fa/admin/config/people/accounts for step 7. (Without Farsi, set Text direction to Right to left instead.)
steps.lookFor: The red bar moves to the right (start) edge, the icon sits at the end of the label, and nothing overlaps.

variants.expected: A closed details section or an inactive vertical tab that contains a field error is visibly marked (red border, icon, red text) and has hidden text " (contains error)" and a data-child-error-count attribute.
variants.actual: Before the change a closed or inactive group gives no sign that a field inside it has an error; the user must open each group to find it.
variants.setup: node tools/compare/setup.mjs 3604037-latest (the environments for a core and the same core with the patch).

observe.label: A group that contains an error (a closed section or an inactive tab) is visibly marked
The mark is more than colour: there is also an icon or a border
The keyboard focus outline on the group is still clearly visible
Anything else looks broken, overlapped or unreadable (borders, icon, text, spacing)

checks.label: Setup reached: the test form shows required-field errors
A group (details) that contains the errors is on the page
The details that contains errors has data-child-error-count
The count is 2 (two required fields inside)
The summary carries the hidden text "(contains error)"
Setup reached: the URL alias error is on the node form
The closed URL alias group is marked (data-child-error-count)
Its summary carries the hidden text "(contains error)"
Setup reached: the account settings form shows an error
A vertical tab that contains an error is marked
That tab has the hidden "(contains error)" text
JavaScript errors on the page (ignoring the harmless "ResizeObserver loop" notice)
Number of open details sections matches the other side

variants.label: #3093378: ARIA disclosure for vertical toolbar submenu buttons (contrib toolbar 2.x, current core main)
variants.description: The toolbar module has moved out of Drupal core into the contrib project 'toolbar'. Both sites run current core main with contrib toolbar 2.x at commit 871ce78 checked out into modules/contrib/toolbar and enabled. Before: the module as-is. After: the module with merge request !6 applied (a real ARIA disclosure: aria-expanded plus a '<name> menu' accessible name, and no text-indent hack). The change is meant to be visually identical, so the difference is in the markup and the accessibility tree, not the pixels.

steps.text: Standard install on current core main with the contrib toolbar module (2.x, commit 871ce78) in modules/contrib and enabled. Default Admin is the admin theme.
Open the home page. The administration toolbar runs across the top of the page.
Open the 'Manage' tray (click the Manage tab in the toolbar).
steps.lookFor: A bar of administration menu links: Content, Structure, Appearance, Extend, Configuration, People, Reports.

steps.text: Expand a section that has a submenu by clicking its disclosure button (the chevron next to 'Structure').
steps.lookFor: The submenu opens. Visually nothing about the button changes: an icon, no visible text.

steps.text: In EACH frame, inspect the disclosure button's markup and accessibility (or press Run checks). Before: a hidden span flips between 'Extend' and 'Collapse' and there is no aria-expanded. After: aria-expanded is 'false' then 'true' and the hidden name is 'Structure menu'.
steps.lookFor: Before the name of the button is the opposite of its state (a toggle label); After the state is separate (aria-expanded) and the name stays 'Structure menu'.

variants.expected: The disclosure button reports its state with aria-expanded and its accessible name is the submenu's link text followed by ' menu' (for example 'Structure menu'). No visual change.
variants.actual: Before, the same button carries no aria-expanded and its name flips between 'Extend' and 'Collapse', conflating the name with the state.

observe.label: The toolbar and its submenu buttons look the same as before the change (same icon, no visible text)
Clicking the disclosure button opens and closes the submenu
The button's state is exposed to assistive tech as aria-expanded
Anything else looks broken, overlapped or different (layout, colours, spacing)

checks.label: Setup reached: the toolbar renders disclosure buttons
A disclosure button carries aria-expanded (the machine-readable state)
The toggle button's label ends with ' menu' (not 'Extend'/'Collapse')
The old 'Extend'/'Collapse' action span is gone
JavaScript errors on the page (ignoring the harmless "ResizeObserver loop" notice)
The same number of disclosure buttons is rendered on both sides

variants.label: #3619154: Sidebar toggle fixes, pinned core
variants.description: MR !16911 reworks the Default Admin node add/edit meta sidebar: sidebar.js is split into a sidebar-toggle SDC + edit-sidebar.js; the toggle and close controls become <button> elements with aria-expanded; open/closed state and width persist across reloads with no flash; below 1024px the overlay content is inert with a focus trap and Escape-to-close; the sidebar is positioned with CSS variables; resizing works after AJAX, with touch and in RTL. Test on a node edit form across widths.

steps.text: Default Admin is the admin theme.
Article content type, the Navigation module and one article node are installed.
Open /node/1/edit (loaded in both frames once you press Go).
Focus the sidebar toggle (top of the meta sidebar) and press the Space key.
steps.lookFor: After: the sidebar toggles. Before: nothing happens — an <a role=button> does not activate on Space.

steps.text: Desktop (>=1024px): toggle the sidebar closed, then reload the frame.
steps.lookFor: After: it stays closed with no flash of the open sidebar. Before: it flashes open on load.

steps.text: Toggle the sidebar open, drag the resize handle, then reload.
steps.lookFor: After: open state and the chosen width persist after reload.

steps.text: Expand a details section in the form.
steps.lookFor: After: the Navigation sidebar does not collapse when content height changes.

steps.text: Narrow the frame below 1024px and open the sidebar.
steps.lookFor: After: focus moves to the close button; Tab stays within the sidebar (content behind is inert); Escape closes it and returns focus to the toggle. The resize handle is hidden below 976px.

variants.expected: After: the toggle and close are <button> elements operable with Enter and Space; aria-expanded tracks the sidebar state; closed/open state and width persist across reloads with no flash; expanding a details element does not collapse Navigation; below 1024px the content under the overlay is inert, focus moves to the close button, and Escape closes the sidebar and returns focus to the toggle. Before: <a href="#" role="button"> controls, Space does not operate them, the sidebar flashes open, and there is no inert overlay or focus trap.
variants.actual: TODO after running
observe: Toggle and close are <button> elements and operable with the Space key (after), vs <a role=button> that ignores Space (before).
aria-expanded on the toggle tracks the open/closed state.
No flash of the open sidebar on load; closed/open state persists across reload.
Desktop: the dragged sidebar width persists after reload; resizing works after AJAX, with touch, and in RTL.
Expanding a details element does not collapse the Navigation sidebar.
Below 1024px: content under the overlay is inert; focus moves to the close button on open; Escape closes the sidebar and returns focus to the toggle.
Sidebar top aligns with the bottom of the top bar (976-1023px and >=1024px); no jump or top-bar overlap on load.
The resize handle is hidden below 976px.

checks.label: Setup reached: the sidebar toggle is on the page
The toggle exposes aria-expanded
The toggle is a real <button> (not an <a role=button>)
The close control is a real <button> (not an <a role=button>)
The close button is the first focusable element in the sidebar (focus order)

variants.description: Toolbar (contrib) orientation toggle icon fails WCAG 1.4.11 (1.7:1). The After side carries the fix: rest icon #bebebe -> #787878 plus a :focus-visible outline. Open the admin toolbar's Manage tray and look at the orientation (push) toggle icon.

steps.text: Core main with the contrib Toolbar module (2.x @ 40434c42) installed.

variants.label: #3415961: [drupalMedia] Using the Insert Media button causes the window to scroll to the bottom of the page, pinned core
variants.description: Open the Insert Media dialog from a CKEditor 5 body field on a tall node form, add an image and press Insert selected, in both frames. Before: the window is reported to jump away from the editor. After (MR !12348): the window should stay where it was. Also try closing the dialog with the X button, which one commenter says the change does not fix.

steps.text: Full HTML uses CKEditor 5 with an Insert Media button, and an Image media type exists.

Open /node/add/article (already loaded in both frames once you press Go). The recipe sets the Body text format to Full HTML, so the Insert Media button is already in the toolbar (Basic HTML has no such button).

Paste about 60 lines into Body so the form is much taller than the frame, then scroll so the editor's top is near the top of the frame. The Save button must be below the fold, or focus cannot scroll the page when the dialog closes and nothing will jump.

Have a small .png or .jpg on your own computer. In EACH frame click Insert Media in the editor toolbar (in a narrow frame it is hidden: click Show more items first), open the Add media tab, upload the image (add alt text if asked), then press Insert selected. A file chooser cannot be mirrored, so do this by hand in each frame.
steps.lookFor: Before is reported to scroll the window away from the editor. After should leave the window where it was. Press Run checks afterwards.

steps.text: Repeat once more, but close the dialog with the X button instead of Insert selected, in each frame.
steps.lookFor: Comment #9 says the page still jumps in this case. Note what you see on each side.

variants.expected: After inserting media from the dialog the window stays where it was and the editor stays in view.
variants.actual: Before, the window is reported to jump after Insert selected. After (MR !12348) it should not. Closing with X may still jump (comment #9, not reproduced).

observe.label: The window jumped away from the editor after Insert selected
The media appears in the editor after Insert selected
The page jumped after closing the dialog with the X button

checks.label: CKEditor 5 on the Body field has the Insert Media (drupalMedia) button configured
The Body editor is still in view after inserting (its top edge is inside the window)
JavaScript errors on the page (ignoring the harmless ResizeObserver loop notice)

variants.label: #3618230: Adopt the ajax MessageCommand for file uploads, pinned core
variants.description: Open /node/add/article in both frames. Upload a .txt file larger than 1 KB to trigger the server-side file size upload error. Before: messages are server-rendered inside the replaced widget prefix directly without using MessageCommand wrapper elements. After (MR !16777): messages are delivered via the AJAX MessageCommand targeting a dedicated container with class file-upload-messages.

steps.text: Article content type with a 1 KB size limit file field exists.
Open /node/add/article in both frames.
Prepare a .txt file on your local machine larger than 1 KB (for example 5 KB).
In EACH frame, select the Attachment file input and upload the oversized file to trigger the server-side validation error AJAX callback.
steps.lookFor: Check if the error message is inserted into a dedicated file-upload-messages container.

variants.expected: The file upload error is rendered using the AJAX MessageCommand targeting the file-upload-messages wrapper container.
variants.actual: Before: messages are directly embedded in the widget prefix response. After: a div with class file-upload-messages is rendered and targeted by MessageCommand.

observe.label: An error message appears after uploading a file larger than 1 KB
The error message is rendered inside a dedicated file-upload-messages container

checks.label: The file input field on the article form exists on the page
The message container added by MR !16777 for MessageCommand targeting exists on the page
No JavaScript errors on the page (ignoring the harmless ResizeObserver loop notice)
